Back then, lawyers criticised the "new" statues as "old wine in a new bottle", largely retaining many problematic provisions introduced in colonial times. Justice Subramonium Prasad observed that the notice was based on the kalandara dated October 17, which consists of the three general diary entries registered at different police stations related to different dates and events. "As such, this Court cannot sit in the armchair of the SEM to test the subjective satisfaction of the sufficiency of material and as to whether the opinion has been correctly been arrived at by the SEM or not," the Bench said. The Court said that the notice, issued under Sections 126 and 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), met the legal requirements for initiating preventive proceedings. The High Court arrived at these findings while dismissing Bora's plea against the notice. items.title: Judge booked for letting minor son drive Mercedes that killed man in Kochi
items.summary: The Juvenile Justice Board in Ernakulam, on Monday, October 26, granted bail to the 17-year-old son of an Additional District Sessions Judge in connection with a fatal accident in Kochi that killed a scooterist in the early hours of Sunday. The judge has also been booked in connection with the accident, as the Mercedes-Benz sedan involved in the crash was registered in his name. According to police, he has been booked under section 199A(1) (holds the guardian or vehicle owner guilty for an offence committed by a juvenile) and 199A(2) (imposes criminal penalties on the guardian or owner, including up to 3 years' imprisonment and a Rs 25,000 fine) of the Motor Vehicles (MV) Act. The minor, who had initially been let go on station bail under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, was taken back into custody due to mounting public pressure and protests by the victim’s family. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has also reportedly been formed to probe allegations made by the victim’s family.
